findings.title: Shell command executes inline script
findings.recommendation: Use a direct, pinned executable instead of a shell wrapper. If a shell is required, place the script in source control and review it.

findings.title: MCP server command includes a dangerous operation
findings.recommendation: Remove the dangerous operation from MCP startup. Run destructive setup steps manually and review them separately.

findings.title: Remote MCP package is not version pinned
findings.recommendation: Pin the package to an exact version such as package@1.2.3 and review updates before changing it.

findings.title: Secret-like environment variable is exposed to MCP server
findings.recommendation: Pass the least privileged token possible. Prefer scoped tokens, short-lived credentials, and a dedicated service account.

findings.title: MCP server has a broad working directory
findings.recommendation: Run the server in a narrow project directory or sandbox with only the files it needs.

findings.title: MCP server argument grants broad filesystem access
findings.recommendation: Replace broad filesystem paths with a dedicated project folder or read-only sandbox path.

findings.title: Secret-like header is configured for remote MCP server
findings.recommendation: Use scoped, short-lived credentials and avoid placing long-lived secrets directly in MCP config files.

findings.title: MCP server is launched through a remote package runner
findings.recommendation: Pin the package version, review the package source, and prefer a local lockfile or vendored executable for sensitive tools.

findings.title: Remote MCP server URL is configured
findings.recommendation: Verify the provider, use HTTPS, document the data sent to this server, and keep an allowlist of approved remote endpoints.
